titulo_es: They would not have had time (or had not, in indirect style)

texto: To refer to an earlier action, **haben/sein** is used in Konjunktiv I + Partizip II: **Er sagt, er habe den Bericht gelesen** (he says he has read the report). **Die Polizei teilt mit, es seien drei Autos beteiligt gewesen** (police report that there were three cars involved). The form of the auxiliary and the context place the action in time; no single «past» of the Konjunktiv I. is used

bloques.titulo: When to replace it with Konjunktiv II
texto: If the form of Konjunktiv I is in line with the sign, Konjunktiv II is usually used to make the above-mentioned speech marked: **Sie sagen, sie kämen morgen** (they say they will come tomorrow). Other strategies, such as **würden** + infinitive, also appear in real use; the choice depends on the registration. The Konjunktiv II also expresses hypotheses: interpose it with the context, not as an automatic brand of indirect style.

frases.de: Die Zeugen sagen, die Fahrer hätten nicht aufgepasst.
frases.es: Los testigos dicen que los conductores no habían prestado atención.
frases.en: Witnesses say the drivers had not paid attention.

frases.de: Die Polizei teilt mit, es seien drei Autos beteiligt gewesen.
frases.es: La policía informa de que había tres coches implicados.
frases.en: The police report that there were three cars involved.

frases.de: Und die Zahl der Verletzten sei gesunken.
frases.es: Y el número de heridos ha bajado.
frases.en: And the number of wounded has fallen.

bloques.pregunta: What form does it serve for the Konjunktiv I of the «haben» (singular) past?

bloques.frase: Sie sagen, sie hätten keine Zeit gehabt.

opciones.texto: They say they haven't had time.
opciones.explicacion: hätten = Konjunktiv II (as well as the Indikative in plural).

opciones.texto: They say they don't have time.
They said they didn't have time.
opciones.explicacion: It's not what the phrase says.

bloques.frase: Die Polizei teilt mit, es ___ drei Autos beteiligt gewesen.

opciones.explicacion: Konjunktiv I of «sein» in plural third person.

bloques.pregunta: What do the witnesses declare according to the sentence?
bloques.frase: Die Zeugen sagen, die Fahrer hätten nicht aufgepasst.

opciones.texto: Witnesses claim that the drivers had not paid attention.
opciones.explicacion: «hätten ... aufgepasst» is the way of past in Konjunktiv for related speech.

opciones.texto: Witnesses claim that the drivers were driving with complete caution.
opciones.explicacion: «nicht aufgepasst» denial indicates lack of attention.

opciones.texto: Los testigos niegan haber presenciado la maniobra de los vehículos.
opciones.explicacion: Witnesses do testify about the lack of attention of drivers.

bloques.pregunta: What is the «haben» Konjunktiv II for «ellos tendrían»?

bloques.frase: Sie sagen, sie ___ den Bericht gelesen.

opciones.explicacion: When the Konjunktiv I («haben») matches the indicative, the Konjunktiv II «hätten» is used.
The «haben» sign does not mark the speech referred to in the third plural person.
«lesen» is a transient verb that forms the composite times with the «haben» auxiliary.

intro: We split two ideas: how to refer to previous facts and what to do when a form of Konjunktiv I coincides with the indicative.
